This is an application filed by the applicant-Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation Ltd. (for short "MSRDC") praying for review of the judgment and order dated 3 rd May 2017 as rendered by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court of which one of us (G. S. Kulkarni, J.)
was a member

entities.text: Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: . There is a delay of 745 days in filing the present application.
On the issue of delay, we have heard Mr.Godbole, learned Counsel for the applicant and Mr.Anturkar, learned Senior Counsel for the respondents-original petitioners.
Having perused the memo of the application, we are of the opinion that there are sufficient reasons made out by the MSRDC for seeking condonation of delay in filing the present Review application.
The delay is hence, condoned.

. We have accordingly heard the learned counsel for the parties on the prayer for review of the judgment and order dated 3rd May 2017.

3. By the judgment under review, Writ Petition no.969 of 2015 filed by Shri.Krishna Bhagwan Kotak and Mrs.Vidya Bhagwan Kotak, the original petitioners against the State of Maharashtra, the Secretary,
Revenue and Forest Department, Mantralaya, Mumbai, the Special Land Acquisition No.2, Mumbai Pune Express Way, Pune, Divisional Commissioner, Pune, and the Collector Pune - the respondents therein,
came to be allowed in terms of the following order:-
 "ORDER  (i) The acquisition proceedings in relation to the  land of the petitioners bearing Gat No. 258 admeasuring 18  Hectors 90 Ares situate at Village Kurwande, Taluka Maval,
 District Pune being the subject matter of acquisition under  notification dated 19 September 1997 issued under Section 6 of  the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 stand lapsed in view of  subsection 2 of Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation  And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation And  Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation  And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation And  Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
(ii) We make it clear that the acquisition would stand lapsed  only in relation to the lands which are subject matter of this  petition and no adjudication is made as regards the legality and  validity of acquisition of other lands if any, which may form  subject matter of the Award.
 (iii) This Order will not preclude the respondents from initiating  fresh acquisition proceedings qua the land in question under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land  Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: (iv) Rule is made absolute accordingly in the above terms.
No  costs."

sentences.text: The original petitioners had contended that as the possession of the land in question was not taken over by the State Government as also the compensation amount being not paid to them, the acquisition of the land in question had lapsed as per the provisions of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.

Such contention as urged by the original petitioners was accepted by this Court in its judgment under review, considering the principles of law, as laid down by the Supreme Court in its decision in Pune Municipal Corporation & Anr. Vs. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki &
Ors. [2014(3) SCC 183] as then applicable and consequently the land acquisition proceedings were set aside.
5.

entities.text:
Pune Municipal Corporation & Anr. Vs. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki &
Ors. [2014(3) SCC 183]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The MSRDC has filed the present review application interalia contending that the acquisition in question was, in fact, at the behest of the MSRDC.

It is contended that after the acquisition process was completed, the possession of the land was also handed over to the MSRDC on 31 March 1998, relying on the panchanama which was also referred to in paragraph 10 of the affidavit in reply filed on behalf of the State Government to the writ petition.
MSRDC has also relied on a Lease Deed dated 11th August 2014 entered by the State Government with the MSRDC, whereby, the land in question was leased in favour of the MSRDC.
A copy of the said Lease Deed is placed on record and annexed as 'Exhibit F' to the present application.

The MSRDC has also relied on the State Government Resolution dated 5 th July 2016, which according to the MSRDC, clearly indicates that, the land in question was  3 of 6  -------------------------

The Court's attention is drawn to "Annexure 2" of the said Government Resolution which states that the possession of the land was handed over to the MSRDC and the same is with the MSRDC.

The MSRDC has also contended that the State Government in paragraph (8) of the affidavit in reply filed in the writ petition of Smt. Harshlata Dhanraj Gedam, Special Land Acquisition Officer No. 1, Pune, had categorically stated that the land acquisition proceedings were completed for public purpose as per Maharashtra State Road Development ... vs Shri. sentences.text:
6. On the above materials, the contention as urged by the MSRDC is to the effect that, despite such clear position that the land in question was acquired at the behest of the MSRDC for the Mumbai-Pune Expressway Project, as also, the possession of the land being handed over to the MSRDC, the petitioners had not impleaded the MSRDC, as a party to the writ petition.
7.

On the above contentions, Mr.Godbole, learned Counsel for the applicant would urge that certainly there was relevant material and circumstances to indicate that the MSRDC was a necessary and a proper party to the writ petition, more particularly, when substantive right, title and interest was created in favour of the MSRDC, qua the acquired land,
as seen from the documents namely the Lease Deed and the Government Resolutions setting out the scheme for transfer of the land in favour of MSRDC, and most importantly, the land in question being in possession of the MSRDC.
8.

On the other hand, Mr.Anturkar, learned Senior Counsel  4 of 6  -------------------------
 11 January 2023 ::: Uploaded on - 23/01/2023 ::: Downloaded on - 29/05/202  pvr 1caw-st-114 appearing for the original petitioners opposed the said application and submitted that, none of the contentions as urged by Mr. Godbole can be considered to be a ground to review the order passed by this Court.

Mr.
Anturkar's contention is that the possession of the land in question has remained with the original petitioners, as also observed by this Court in the order under review.

Mr. Anturkar's contention is also that the Lease Deed as also the Government Resolution dated 10 th December 2007 and the Government Resolution dated 5 th July 2016 would not assist the applicant to demonstrate any vested legal rights of the applicant on the land in question.
9. We have heard learned Counsel for the parties, we have also perused the record.

On perusal of the memo of the application as also the Lease Deed dated 11th August 2014 as also the Government Resolution dated 10th December 2007 and the subsequent Government Resolution dated 5th July 2016, we are not persuaded to accept Mr.
Anturkar's submission that no legal rights whatsoever were vested with the MSRDC in respect of the acquired land and subject matter of the Maharashtra State Road Development ... vs Shri. Krishna Bhagwan Kotak And Ors on 11 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117755972/
4 proceedings.

entities.text: Maharashtra State Road Development ... vs Shri. Krishna Bhagwan Kotak And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On examining these documents, we are quite certain that the MSRDC was a necessary and proper party to the writ petition, hence,
the MSRDC ought to have been impleaded and heard in the adjudication of the writ petition.

For such reason, we are of the clear opinion that the impugned judgment and order dated 3 rd May 2017 is required to be recalled by permitting the petitioners to implead the MSRDC as a party to the writ petition for the appropriate adjudication of the writ petition.

10. We, accordingly, allow this review application, by passing the following order:-
 5 of 6  -------------------------
 11 January 2023 ::: Uploaded on - 23/01/2023 ::: Downloaded on - 29/05/202  pvr 1caw-st  ORDER (i) The impugned judgment and order under review, dated 3rd May 2017 is recalled.
(ii) Writ Petition No.969 of 2015 is restored to the file of this Court.
(iii) Writ Petition be placed before the regular Court for its adjudication.
(iv) All contentions of the parties on merits of the writ petition are expressly kept open.
11. Civil Application is disposed of in the above terms.
No costs.
